messages.subject: modification indices WLSMV
parts:
Dear all, 
I used the WLSMV estimator for testing measurement invariance. 
In testing for strong measurement invariance (equal factor loadings and thresholds), the delta/CFI was lower than the recommend threshold (see Cheung & Rensvold, 2000).
When I used the MODINDICES command, there are no threshhold modification indices. How can I see which item do I have to release? Or how can I test for partial strong invariance?
Thank you very much for your help.

Akhtar

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: modification indices WLSMV
parts: In testing for strong measurement invariance (equal factor loadings and thresholds), the delta/CFI was lower than the recommend threshold (see Cheung & Rensvold, 2000).

That threshold is invalid:

http://www.tandfonline.com/doi/abs/10.1080/10705511.2014.882658

Permutation is a possible solution, which is available in the semTools package:

https://doi.org/10.1037/met0000152
When I used the MODINDICES command, there are no threshhold modification indices. How can I see which item do I have to release?

Because you are already estimating all of your thresholds.  The modindices() function only returns indices for parameters that are fixed to a certain value (e.g., zero).  If you want indices to test equality constraints, use the lavTestScore() function.  You can compare the constraints in the output to those in the parTable() or summary() output to see how to adjust your syntax.  You can read more details I posted here:

https://groups.google.com/d/msg/lavaan/l5aUQfvcZT4/S_uGCAhICAAJ
